summary: Lunar Eye is an easy to use and intuitive lunar mission planning software designed to simulate, visualize, and predict space missions around the Moon. It allows users to explore possible mission trajectories, analyze orbital paths, and understand the complex dynamics involved in lunar exploration. By combining realistic 3D visualizations of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with mission planning tools, Lunar Eye provides an accessible yet powerful environment for designing and studying lunar missions. Whether for educational purposes, scientific research, or space exploration enthusiasts, Lunar Eye aims to make orbital mechanics and mission planning easier to understand and explore.
details:
Lunar Eye – 3D Solar System Simulator and Lunar Mission Planner

Lunar Eye is an interactive 3D space exploration and mission planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Its main goal is to make lunar mission planning more accessible, understandable and scientifically accurate by combining real astronomical data, orbital mechanics, terrain analysis and 3D visualization.

The software allows users to explore the Solar System in 3D, visualize the positions of planets, the Earth, the Moon and other celestial objects, and investigate potential lunar landing sites.

One of its main features is the Lunar Explorer, which uses real elevation data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LOLA) to create a 3D representation of the Moon's surface. Users can select potential landing locations and analyze important characteristics such as elevation, terrain slope and the local horizon.

The Mission Planning section allows users to study environmental conditions at a selected lunar location and during a specific time window. It calculates when the Sun and Earth are visible from the surface, taking the surrounding lunar terrain into account. It also estimates illumination periods and the potential energy production of solar panels. An interactive timeline helps users understand how these conditions change over time.

Another important feature is the ability to compare different candidate landing sites, helping users evaluate which locations may be more suitable for future lunar missions. Results can also be exported as CSV and PDF files for further analysis and documentation.

Scientific approach and technologies

A fundamental aspect of Lunar Eye is its use of real scientific data rather than artificially generated astronomical positions. The project integrates:

  • NASA/JPL Horizons API: provides accurate astronomical positions and orbital information for celestial objects.
  • NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LOLA): provides lunar elevation data used to reconstruct the Moon's terrain.
  • DE441 ephemerides: supports precise calculations of celestial body positions.
  • IAU 2015 orientation models: used for planetary and lunar orientation.

The project was developed using Python, JavaScript, HTML and CSS. The backend uses FastAPI to handle scientific calculations and data retrieval, while the frontend uses Three.js for 3D visualization and Chart.js for interactive graphs and timelines. NumPy supports numerical calculations, and Docker is used to simplify deployment and application management.

Benefits and intended impact

Lunar Eye aims to make the complex process of planning lunar missions easier to understand and explore. By combining scientific data with an accessible visual interface, it can help students, educators and space enthusiasts learn about orbital mechanics, lunar geography and the environmental challenges of operating on the Moon.

It also demonstrates why selecting a lunar landing site involves much more than finding a flat area: sunlight availability, terrain obstacles, visibility of Earth and energy generation are all important factors that must be considered.

Creativity and innovation

What makes Lunar Eye creative is the integration of several different scientific disciplines into a single interactive platform. Instead of presenting astronomical information through static images or isolated datasets, it transforms real scientific information into an explorable 3D environment connected directly to practical mission planning tools.

The project connects Solar System visualization, lunar surface reconstruction, environmental analysis and educational experimentation, allowing users to move from exploring celestial objects to investigating realistic lunar mission scenarios.

Factors considered during development

During development, we considered several important factors:

  • Scientific reliability: prioritizing real NASA and JPL datasets and validating calculations against reference astronomical data.
  • Mission feasibility: considering illumination, terrain elevation, slopes and visibility conditions when evaluating landing locations.
  • Accessibility: creating an intuitive interface suitable for users with different levels of scientific and technical knowledge.
  • Performance: managing large terrain datasets and astronomical calculations efficiently.
  • Transparency: distinguishing between real measurements, interpolated values and approximations, while avoiding fabricated results when data is unavailable.
  • Educational value: making complex scientific concepts easier to explore through interactive visualizations.

Ultimately, Lunar Eye aims to bridge the gap between scientific data and practical space exploration, giving everyone the opportunity to explore the challenges of planning a mission to the Moon.
